description: canonical_bytes(subject) for subject.context-snapshot/1 (verifier-toolkit/1 §8.5 + subject.context-snapshot/1 §7): the subject is exactly the payload.snapshot JSON value, canonicalized as the UTF-8 bytes of its RFC 8785 (JCS) serialization. Per §7.1, every numeric-looking value MUST be carried as a JSON string and the object MUST contain no JSON number token at any depth, so RFC 8785 number serialization never applies — JCS reduces to deterministic key ordering and string escaping, which conforming JCS libraries implement identically across languages. Array order is significant (JCS does not reorder). subject_local_digest_hex = SHA3-256(canonical_bytes).
canonicalization: RFC 8785 JCS of the payload.snapshot value; all numeric-looking fields are strings (no JSON number tokens); array order preserved
digest: subject_local_digest_hex = SHA3-256(canonical_bytes), 32 bytes lowercase hex; verifier-local, never published

vectors.name: all-strings snapshot with ordered entries array
array order is significant: same entries reversed -> different digest (contrast with vector 1)
UTF-16 code-unit key sort: a supplementary-plane key sorts by its high surrogate (below U+E000), NOT by code point
vectors.note: RFC 8785 §3.2.3 sorts keys by UTF-16 code unit. U+1F600 encodes as the surrogate pair D83D DE00; its first code unit 0xD83D is BELOW the BMP key U+E000, so the order is 'z' (007A) < U+1F600 < U+E000. A code-point sort would place U+E000 (57344) before U+1F600 (128512) and produce different bytes. This is the one documented case where a naive code-point sort diverges cross-language; pin it.

negative_cases.name: JSON number token -> non-conformant
negative_cases.why: a JSON number token anywhere violates the string-only discipline; the profile does not apply (SubjectPreconditionError)

negative_cases.name: number nested inside an array -> non-conformant (depth-recursive)
negative_cases.why: the string-only discipline is recursive; a number at any depth (here inside a nested array) is non-conformant

must_hold: the subject is exactly payload.snapshot (not the enclosing payload, not a subset)
JCS sorts object keys by UTF-16 code unit per RFC 8785; array order is NOT sorted and is significant
a supplementary-plane key sorts by its UTF-16 high surrogate, NOT by code point (see the UTF-16 vector)

every numeric-looking value is a string; a JSON number token anywhere makes the object non-conformant (the profile does not apply and the implementation MUST fail closed); booleans and nulls are preserved as such (see positive_cases)
two snapshots with identical content but different array order produce different canonical bytes and are distinct snapshots

positive_cases.name: CCVP/1 7.1 normative entry shape
positive_cases.why: the governing protocol's own entry example: an open-ended eligibility window is a JSON null, and CCVP/1 8 reads `entry.valid_to is not null`. Spelling it as a string would be the coercion subject.context-snapshot/1 8 forbids

positive_cases.name: booleans and nulls are preserved, not coerced
positive_cases.why: 7 requires preserving the exact string, boolean, array, object and null semantics of the input. Both canonicalize identically across languages under RFC 8785 - unlike numbers, they are not a divergence vector

positive_cases.name: key ordering and non-ASCII strings
positive_cases.why: JCS sorts by UTF-16 code unit and escapes minimally; string content is preserved byte-for-byte
